# Online Store Sales Visualization Plan

A compact chart set will show **seasonality**, **top products**, and **month-to-month growth** clearly from Jan–Apr 2025.

## Best 3 Charts for Category Sales Trends

| Chart | Best Use | What it Should Highlight |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-line trend chart | Seasonality across months | Compare T-shirts, Hoodies, and Hats over time; spot peaks and dips quickly |
| Ranked bar chart | Top-performing products | Show total units sold by category to identify the best seller overall |
| Month-over-month growth chart | Growth momentum | Show which categories accelerated or slowed from one month to the next |

## Recommended Chart Set

### 1) Multi-line Trend Chart
- **X-axis:** Month
- **Y-axis:** Units sold
- **Series:** T-shirts, Hoodies, Hats
- **Key insight:** T-shirts lead every month and all categories rise into March, suggesting a strong spring lift; April shows a small pullback for T-shirts and Hoodies while Hats continue to improve.

### 2) Ranked Bar Chart
- **X-axis:** Category
- **Y-axis:** Total units sold across Jan–Apr
- **Key insight:** T-shirts are the clear top performer, with Hoodies second and Hats third; this makes the product mix easy to prioritize for inventory and promotions.

### 3) Month-to-Month Growth Chart
- **X-axis:** Month
- **Y-axis:** % change vs prior month, or absolute unit change
- **Series:** One line per category or grouped bars by category
- **Key insight:** Growth is strongest from February to March for all categories, especially T-shirts; April reveals moderation, which may indicate seasonality or demand normalization.

## Quick Actions

- Data visualization principles: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/visualizations/
